children: Gold futures fell slightly in rangebound trading Tuesday as traders lowered exposure a day ahead of U.S. Consumer Price Index data and its implications for Federal Reserve interest rate policy.
The dollar and benchmark 10-year Treasury ​yields slipped from their ​respective highs but ⁠still hovered near elevated levels, while oil prices ended mixed.
Traders currently see only ‌a ⁠19% chance of a Fed rate hike this month but are pricing in an 88% chance of a December increase, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

"Expectations of an October Fed rate hike remained subdued ahead of U.S. economic data this week, but markets are still pricing in a strong chance of a hike in December, [which] could keep gold at risk," Critical Metals CEO Tony Sage said in a note.
Softer CPI or PPI numbers this week could help gold rebound, but "stronger-than-expected prints may lift the dollar and yields, pushing the yellow metal lower," Sage also said.

Gold has fallen ~5% since early September as persistent inflation concerns revived expectations of further Fed rate hikes, but much of the bad news for gold has been priced in as expectations of an October Fed rate hike ease, UBS head of China basic materials research Sharon Ding said in a note.

"We see greater scope for stabilization if incoming data no longer justify further upward revisions to the expected policy path," Ding wrote, adding that a sustained retreat in Treasury yields could also strengthen the case for gold's recovery.
